applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Agreement between Canada and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; United Nations Act, SC 1992, c 17; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 10; BC Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, s 57; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp.), s 233.3; FINTRAC regulations under the PCMLTFA; BC Registry issued Beneficial Ownership guidelines stipulating an 'individual with significant control' disclosure register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport / national identity document for each director, officer, and individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office / civil registry of the UBO's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of issuance and, if required, Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization through the Canada Mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of current residential address for each UBO and director (utility bill or bank statement, issued within the last 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy and, where applicable, Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal record certificate from country of nationality and all countries of prior residence for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police service or ministry of interior of the issuing country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Canadian Consular Legalization after competent authority authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and professional standing for each individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Exceptionally, a financial institution where the UBO holds an account; where relevant a foreign equivalent of a FINTRAC reporting entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization only if demanded by the Canadian corporate registry or financial institution review

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, and current shareholder register for each intermediate corporate shareholder in the UBO ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry / registrar of companies of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for jurisdictions party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the Canadian Embassy or Consulate plus Global Affairs Canada authentication

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and every individual with significant control against the FINTRAC administrative directives; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions guidance; Canadian domestic sanctions lists promulgated by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; UN Security Council Consolidated List; and, because USD clearing and cross-border escrow funding are contemplated, the OFAC SDN List as a secondary but practically essential reference. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, for any person residing in or funded from a FATF high-risk jurisdiction, and for all clients engaging the study-abroad/immigration-advisory business model. Source of funds must be documented, suspicious or attempted transactions must result in a Suspicious Transaction Report to FINTRAC, and any debarment, visa-refusal, or immigration-related sanction action must be identified before incorporation.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_comment: The register is maintained privately by the corporation and is available to domestic authorities upon lawful demand; it is not a fully public UBO register in British Columbia.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries (bcregistry.ca) / BC Corporate Registry Online
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in British Columbia must use Latin characters and ordinarily include English or French wording. A non-Latin script name is permitted only as an informal transliterated secondary use; the statutory registered name must be the romanized/transliterated Latin-character version. The proposed name must be 'distinguishable' as provided under the BC Business Corporations Act and the Name Regulation, and it must not be confusingly similar to any existing BC, extra-provincial, or federal corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC name reservation expires 56 days after issuance; no statutory extension is available after expiry, and a new name request must be submitted. If the name examiner rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the BC Registrar within 30 days of the refusal, stating specifically why the proposed name is distinguishable and compliant with the Name Regulation. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may file a fresh name request, resubmit under a different corporate form, or commence judicial review of the Registrar's decision in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c 241. Practical advice for the immigration/study-abroad sector: obtain a pre-clearance opinion from local counsel before reserving a name because names suggesting unlicensed academic, fiduciary, or government functions are highly likely to be refused.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office / corporate service provider may be used as the registered office only if the provider maintains a physical street address in British Columbia, accepts service of process during normal business hours, and holds the statutory records at an accessible BC records address. A post office box alone is prohibited. For a study-abroad and immigration/visa consultancy regulated by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants or a provincial education-agent regime, the regulator expects substantive client-facing business premises in British Columbia; reliance solely on a virtual office for the principal operational place of business would materially increase regulatory risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate; approximately 25-35% annual likelihood because this activity sits in FINTRAC's 'money services / international transfer' adjacent risk profile and because immigration-consulting regulators and municipal business licensing authorities conduct unannounced physical inspections, especially when client files, escrow accounts, or immigration form preparation are involved.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC Name Search, Name Reservation, and NUANS-equivalent Examination Fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published statutory registry tariff; Name Reservation fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC Business Corporation Incorporation Filing Fee (online incorporation under BC Business Corporations Act)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published statutory registry tariff for filing under the BC Business Corporations Act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate organizational and legal services (drafting articles, organizational resolutions, minute book, share certificates, BC records office review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Counsel / licensed paralegal or BC corporate legal service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard BC private business corporation incorporation and minute book organization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered and records office service fee (initial annual fee by BC service-provider law firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a physical BC registered office address and statutory records custody

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing analysis and initial register of individuals with significant control (ISC) compliance setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee market benchmark; includes 25% threshold analysis, control-in-fact review, and domestic/foreign sanctions screening documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT internal compliance manual, FINTRAC reporting procedures, escrow/wire-transfer protocols, and PEP screening policy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent AML law firm or certified AML consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing expert market fee for a medium-risk immigration/study-abroad consulting entity with escrow account usage

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille, consular legalization, and certified translation of foreign UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Global Affairs Canada (authentication), and Canadian embassy/consulate where consular legalization is required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary/commissioner schedule and prevailing apostille/consular fee benchmark; actual cost varies with document count and issuing country

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal business license pre-clearance / pre-incorporation regulatory eligibility assessment (immigration consultant CICC licensing prerequisite review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: City or municipal licensing department (e.g., City of Vancouver) and regulatory advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal business licence fee assessment and market advisory fee; CICC licensing examination is not included at Stage 1

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 (BCBCA), especially ss. 10-13 (incorporation), 22 (certificate of incorporation), 24-28 (memorandum and articles), and 190 (registered office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies — BC Registry Services, Corporate Online Division, Ministry of Citizen Services, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles, submitted electronically via Corporate Online together with the Incorporation Application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the BCBCA; shares may be issued for nominal consideration, e.g. CAD 1.00 per common share. No escrow or paid-in capital deposit is required where the corporation is not distributing securities under a prospectus.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the share subscription of the initial common shareholders, as listed in the subscription schedule, is hereby accepted and the Board directs the issuance of one common share per subscriber against payment of CAD 1.00, fully paid and non-assessable. 2. THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address set out in the Notice of Articles, and the Corporate Registry be notified of any change. 3. THAT the appointed Director be confirmed and the President, Secretary and sole signing officer be appointed, with authority to execute all banking, CRA and regulatory filings. 4. THAT the corporate seal and share certificate form be adopted as presented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services — Corporate Online Name Request Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through an approved service provider, then submit a Name Request through Corporate Online. Ensure the proposed name contains a distinct element, a descriptive element, and a legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' The reservation is valid for 56 days from approval.
required_dossiers: NUANS Search Report (recent, dated within 4 months)
Corporate name consent letter, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a response within 14 days through Corporate Online, request reconsideration, or submit an alternative name. Conflicts with existing BC trade marks may require a consent letter or a revised name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies — Corporate Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Incorporation Application together with the Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles via Corporate Online. Pay the applicable filing fee by credit card or EFI. Specify the effective date and time of incorporation. Verify the registered records office address and first director information prior to submission.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles (Form 1) executed by incorporator
Articles of Incorporation (custom or model articles under Part 2 CBCA)
Consent of first director to act as director (Form 5, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a requisition, correct the deficiencies and refile within 14 days. If the filing fee payment is rejected, resubmit using an alternative payment method. Incorporation takes effect only upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / Canada Revenue Agency OneStart Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, register through CRA OneStart to obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN), corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and payroll account if employees are expected. Filing under OneStart is mandatory for integrating federal and provincial accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the BC Registrar
WorkSafeBC registration form if hiring employees
CRA RC105 'Directors' Direct Deposit' Request, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN registration is delayed, contact the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525 and provide the Corporate Online Registry ID and incorporation date. Errors in the BN account setup can be corrected by filing an RC-account adjustment or by calling the CRA officer with the Corporation's legal name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Corporate Records Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services / Corporate Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt a written resolution, execute the first board resolution, issue share certificates to subscribers, appoint officers, and establish a records office at the registered address in British Columbia. File Notice of Change of Directors (Form 10) within 15 days if any officer or director differs from the initial filing.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office access documents
Form 10 Notice of Change of Directors/Officers, if any changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the records are deficient, remedy by executing a supplemental resolution and updating the corporate register. Late filing of Form 10 attracts late filing penalties; the filing can be cured by submission with payment of the applicable late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Licensing and AML Compliance for Study Abroad and Immigration Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) / FINTRAC / Consumer Protection BC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licence for each advising principal under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act. Register the corporation as a money services business with FINTRAC if it remits funds for clients, and enrol with the designated client compensation fund for client funds held. If operating an agency that recruits international students for BC institutions, execute the BC International Student Program registration with the BC Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills.
required_dossiers: Valid RCIC licence certificates for all immigration advisors
FINTRAC MSB registration confirmation, if applicable
Client trust account and escrow agreements
Consumer Protection BC registration, if engaging in student recruitment for BC institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CICC imposes conditions or undertakings, remedy through completion of mandatory continuing professional development and submission of supplementary declarations. Appeals are available under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act, and recurring deficiencies may be escalated for disciplinary review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) for regulated immigration consulting; Consumer Protection BC for international student placement agency registration in British Columbia
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licence under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act, SC 2019 c 29, s 292, together with a BC municipal business licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy — Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-only professional advisory services with no listed activity triggers under the BC Environmental Assessment Act and its Reviewable Projects Regulation; no environmental impact assessment required for office leasing, document storage and consultancy operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for office operations. For sanitary wastewater, comply with municipal sewer bylaws under the BC Public Health Act; for commercial waste, comply with the Recycling Regulation (BC Reg 449/2004) respecting paper, electronics and packaging. No significant VOC or combustion emissions sources exist beyond routine HVAC maintenance, which must follow mechanical maintenance standards under the BC Fire Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification must be obtained from the local fire authority or the Provincial Fire Commissioner under the Fire Safety Act and BC Fire Code, including an occupancy inspection for the leased office premises. Structural load clearance is required from the municipality or the building owner confirming the floor design load is adequate for the office use. WorkSafeBC registration and employer occupational health and safety clearance are mandatory under the Workers Compensation Act, including completion of the employer registration, injury reporting protocol, and a first-aid assessment for the work premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – Business Registration Online portal (canada.ca/business-registration-online)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity carrying on business in Canada must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA’s Business Registration Online, or by submitting Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), and may concurrently register for GST/HST, corporate income tax, payroll, and other program accounts. Non-resident corporations without a permanent establishment may still require a BN for withholding, excise, or GST/HST purposes if Canadian-source activities exist. For British Columbia, a separate PST registration is required with the BC Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime. The entity's legal form determines tax classification. Certain elections exist under the Income Tax Act, including the subsection 216(1) election for non-residents on Canadian rental income, the subsection 216(4) election, deemed-disposition elections under subsection 128(1), and hybrid mismatch elections under sections 18.2 and 18.3 to align Canadian and foreign tax treatment of structured arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) under the Provincial Sales Tax Act; BC Employer Health Tax (EHT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST small-supplier threshold is CAD 30,000. A non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada may be required to register regardless of threshold if carrying on business in Canada or soliciting orders through an agent. BC PST registration is required for sellers making taxable retail sales in British Columbia; BC EHT registration threshold is annual BC payroll of CAD 500,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No universal real-time fiscal clearance mandate. Canada supports voluntary PEPPOL-based e-invoicing (Pan-Canadian e-invoice framework, PEPPOL BIS 3.0). CRA does not require pre-clearance API submission or digital fiscal stamping. BC PST requires displayed PST registration number and prescribed invoice data, but no provincial real-time clearance platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V, section 1 of the Excise Tax Act applies to supplies of goods exported by a registrant to a non-resident, and services supplied to a non-resident where the service is not consumed in Canada. Study-abroad immigration and visa advisory services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient, provided the recipient is not resident in Canada, the service is not an exempt financial service, and the service is not made available for consumption in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Cargo Export Declaration via Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS)
Export permit or licence under the Export and Import Permits Act (if applicable)
Bill of Lading or airway waybill evidencing export
Commercial invoice with zero-rating notation and GST/HST registration number
Proof of settlement (wire transfer, SWIFT confirmation, bank statement or inward remittance certificate)
Contract and supporting correspondence showing non-resident recipient status
Detailed evidence that the service was performed outside Canada for non-resident end consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years, or ten years if misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default is established. Denial of zero-rating or input tax credits triggers repayment of tax, interest under the Excise Tax Act, and a 25% penalty for false or fraudulent claims under section 285. Criminal prosecution under section 327 for evasion may result in fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. Provincial PST and EHT authorities impose separate interest, penalties, and director liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully convertible currency regime under the Exchange Control Act administered by the Bank of Canada. Current account transactions, including profit remittances, consulting fees, and service payments, are freely convertible without prior approval. Capital account transactions require notification or approval from the Bank of Canada or OSFI only in limited cases involving significant foreign direct investment or portfolio flows exceeding CAD 100 million annually. Profit remittance for Canadian corporations is unrestricted subject to corporate tax filing, beneficial ownership disclosure, and anti-money laundering verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canadian exporters are not subject to mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Banks may request supporting documentation for Income Tax Act compliance and anti-money laundering purposes. No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies; voluntary surrender through spot or forward contracts is permitted at the exporter's discretion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions such as Wise and Revolut maintain limited cross-border viability in Canada under the Payment Services Act and FINTRAC regulations. Offshore digital EMIs are constrained by licensing requirements and must partner with domestically regulated Canadian payment service providers. Full remote issuance without local presence is generally prohibited for corporate clients handling volumes above CAD 50,000 monthly.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors, officers, and authorized signatories must attend in-person KYC interviews at a branch in British Columbia for initial corporate account onboarding. Remote account opening is permitted solely for subsequent transactions following successful initial verification; new corporate entity setups require physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds from foreign clients or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client service agreements, immigration application records, tax invoices, source of wealth statements, beneficial ownership certificates, and regulatory approvals

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership or politically exposed persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence reports, independent verification of identity documents, and senior management approval

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 899 (Consulting Services) or 899 (Fee for Services). All wires require matching beneficiary details to the corporate bank account, supporting documentation of service agreements, tax invoices, and client immigration visa application numbers for traceability. Verification protocols mandate dual approval by treasury and compliance teams.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements processed through SWIFT MT103 for commercial payments or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit via correspondent banks. Disbursements to foreign suppliers or clients require prior treasury authorization and compliance sign-off to ensure sanctions screening compliance and proper purpose coding.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for Asian currency pairs
Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, s. 51)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Corporate Registry, administered by the Land Title and Survey Authority of BC (LTSA), Victoria, British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two (2) months after the annual anniversary of incorporation; e.g., a company incorporated on 15 March must file on or before 14 May each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing causes 'delinquent' status on the day after the deadline; the Registrar may administratively strike off and dissolve the corporation after two consecutive missed annual reports and notice. Directors continue to have duties during delinquency; restoration requires a resolution, reinstatement application and an additional restoration fee (approx. CAD 100–500), and property of a dissolved company escheats to the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 150)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar year-end (31 December), the return is due by 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, doubled to 10% and 2% per month for a repeat failure within three years; compound daily interest applies on unpaid balances; CRA may issue an arbitrary assessment for unfiled years and may enforce by garnishment, lien and director-liability proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST (5% federal) Annual Return — annual remitter election (Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15, s. 238)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST Program, Ottawa, Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end for an annual remitter (e.g., 31 December year-end due 31 March next year); monthly/quarterly remitters use one-month/one-month-and-15-day? Actually quarterly returns due within one month after quarter-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equals 5% of net tax owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; simple/composition? interest is charged on net tax remitted late; directors may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST that was collected or should have been collected; chronic failure can trigger an arbitrary assessment under ETA s. 299.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CICC annual licence renewal and declaration for the designated Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) (College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act, S.C. 2019, c. 29) — sector-specific to ISIC 7810/NAICS 541199
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC), Toronto, Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the expiry date on the RCIC certificate; the College sets the renewal cycle (open in the 60 days preceding expiry); the corporation may only provide immigration services while a licensed RCIC is in good standing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of the RCIC designation suspends all immigration representation work; continued practice without a valid licence is a statutory offence under the CICC Act and may lead to administrative penalties, disciplinary suspension or revocation, cancellation of professional liability insurance, and the corporation must immediately reassign client files to another active RCIC.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold is prescribed by the BCBCA. Every BC company must appoint an auditor unless all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment by written approval or by a unanimous shareholder agreement. A mandatory independent audit is triggered when the corporation is a reporting issuer, when its articles/unanimous shareholder agreement so require, or when a sectoral regulator or financier contractually requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; a private BC business corporation may elect International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). ASPE is the standard default for a small private study-abroad/immigration consultancy; if consolidated parent uses IFRS, IFRS is typical. Financial statements must be prepared annually and presented to shareholders; the federal tax return (T2) follows the Income Tax Act computation and CRA-specified forms.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BCBCA transparency register: the corporation must maintain an internal register of 'significant individuals' (any individual holding 25% or more of voting shares or with de facto control). On a share transfer or allotment that changes significant control, the register must be amended within 15 days after the corporation becomes aware of the change. Annually, during the preparation of the BC Annual Report, directors must confirm the accuracy of the register and record the confirmation in the minute book. The transparency register is available on lawful request to the Registrar, the RCMP, CSIS and designated AML authorities, but it is not filed as a public document with the BC Corporate Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Accounting records and signed annual financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.0% combined for a corporation that is not a CCPC (15.0% federal Part I general rate plus 12.0% British Columbia general corporate income tax rate); 11.0% combined (9.0% federal plus 2.0% BC) for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist under the Income Tax Act (Canada); rate relief is available through the CCPC small business deduction (9% federal + 2% BC), the scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (15%-35%), accelerated capital cost allowance, the foreign tax credit for foreign-source income, and certain provincial non-refundable credits; a corporation whose voting control is held by non-residents is excluded from CCPC status and cannot claim the small business deduction.
